intent: Preserve the full claim set of the source at a lower word count. Unlike summarize, nothing is dropped for priority — everything is said more densely.
must_preserve: every claim the source makes, not a prioritized subset
attribution, numbers, and stated uncertainty for every claim
the relative weight the source gave each claim

new_claims.rationale: Compression is a density operation on existing claims, not a selection or synthesis operation.

source_fidelity.rationale: The full claim set survives; only the words used to carry it shrink.

structure_rule: Compression may combine sentences and remove redundant restatement, but it may not remove a claim to hit a length target — that is summarize, not compress.
verification_burden: verify-claims checks that the compressed count of distinct claims matches the source's count; a shrinking claim count under this transformation is a defect, not an efficiency.
anti_patterns: Dropping a minor claim because it did not fit the word budget (this is summarize mislabeled as compress)
Merging two distinct claims into one sentence in a way that blurs which evidence supports which
Compressing a hedge until it reads as certain
Using compression to justify cutting attribution
